subject: POC proposal: latency/throughput/cost/quality success criteria & owners
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.inference>
To: Samira Khan <samira.k@quantumpay.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.inference>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.inference>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.inference>
Date: 2026-08-29T14:12:00-07:00
Subject: POC proposal: latency/throughput/cost/quality success criteria & owners

Hi Samira — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick concise recap and a proposed POC plan so we can lock the kickoff: 

Summary of ask
- Evaluate Redwood inference for QuantumPay invoice-parsing and enrichment pipeline (entity extraction + normalization).
- Key constraints: 95th pct latency under real-time route, handle peak bursts during settlement windows, and keep cost per token compatible with your margin targets.

Proposed POC (4 weeks) — high level
- Week 0 (prep): data exchange + access (you provide 5k sample invoices; Redwood reads on S3).
- Week 1: integration + baseline runs (single-model, default quantization).
- Week 2: stress/throughput and instrumentation (batching, KV cache, autoscale).
- Week 3: quality readout and tuning (prompt templates, sampling, reranking).
- Week 4: acceptance window + ops handoff.

Success criteria (explicit, measurable)
- Latency: 95th percentile tail < 250ms for single-request latency on our reserved route (target 200ms if we can).
- Throughput: sustain 1,000 requests/min with 95% success rate during a 10-minute window (burst to 2,500 requests/min supported with fallback model).
- Cost: average cost/token <= $0.0025 for production-like workload (we'll run representative token-distribution runs to confirm).
- Quality: automated precision/recall on entity extraction >= 90% F1 on your labeled subset; human review pass-rate >= 92% on a 200-sample blind set.

Operational commitments and owners
- Integration & infra: Monica Patel (CS) — S3 ingestion, route setup, and logs.
- Model/perf tuning: Rishi Malhotra (ML Eng) — kernel selection, quantization suggestions.
- Commercial & SLA: me (Ben Carter) — deal coordination, pricing.
- Exec escalation: Laura Bennett (Sales Manager) — SLA exceptions.

Attachments: I’ve attached a short data-specs workbook and an ops-runbook draft for review.

Next steps
1) Samira: confirm sample data availability and whether we need an NDA addendum for sample transfer.
2) QuantumPay: provide a preferred kickoff week (we penciled in Sep 7).
3) Internal: Monica/Rishi to review ops-runbook and flag any missing infra requirements by Tue.

Thanks — I’ll hold the Sep 7 slot tentatively until I hear back.

Best,
Ben
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.inference

Ben — thanks for the clear plan, this looks good and close to what we discussed. Quick clarifications from our side: 

1) Data & privacy\- We can share a 5k sample set but need a one-page addendum confirming samples won't be used to train models outside the POC and will be deleted after 90 days. Is that something Redwood can sign?

2) SOC2 evidence & SSO\- Procurement will want a SOC2 report and to confirm SSO (SAML) support before production. Can Monica or Rishi point me to where we can get those docs?

3) Kickoff\- Sep 7 works for our engineering team, but we’d like a concrete ops runbook itemizing S3 prefixes and IAM roles before then.

If you can get the one-page addendum and ops checklist to me by Sep 3, I’ll route to legal & procurement. Also looping in our engineering lead offline.

—Samira

Thanks Samira / Ben — internal ops follow-up and checklist (Monica owner):

Checklist (deliverables before Sep 7 kickoff)
- Legal: one-page data addendum drafted (Ben -> Legal).
- Security: SOC2 report + summary link (I’ll attach next).
- Access: S3 prefixes + ephemeral IAM role for onboarding (Samira to confirm path; I’ll provide role template).
- Networking: we’ll provision a dedicated VPC route (if requested) — initial plan uses hosted route with private routing.
- Metrics / instrumentation: we will ship Prometheus + OpenTelemetry counters for latency/throughput and a small dashboard in Redwood Console.
- Evaluation harness: small harness to run the 5k sample and return per-field precision/recall, latency distributions, and per-token cost estimates. Rishi to own ML config.

Ops cadence and owners
- Day -5 (prep): Legal addendum + S3 path confirmed (Ben/Samira).
- Day 0 (kickoff): access granted, baseline run completed (Monica).
- Day 7 (readout 1): latency & throughput stress test results (Rishi + Monica).
- Day 14 (readout 2): quality tuning, human review batch (Samira + Monica).
- Day 21 (acceptance): final quality & cost signoff (Ben + Samira).

Notes on targets (we’ll make these measurable in the runbook)
- Instrumentation will log tokens/request and compute cost-per-request using our current pricing table; we’ll include both total tokens and tokens billed (prompt+completion).
- For latency runs we’ll run both 1:1 real-time calls and batched runs to show tradeoffs; will publish p50/p95/p99 distributions.

Attachments to follow: SOC2 summary, IAM role template. I’ll also upload the ops-runbook v0 to the shared Drive link Ben included.

Monica Patel
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwood.inference
